entries.title: Expand leading home-directory paths in MCP tools
entries.rationale: Accept the consistency goal for explicitly requested paths, but do not adopt unrestricted home-directory access wording or behavior. Zion must preserve tool/policy authorization, prevent recursive expansion, and keep user/channel content untrusted.
security_reasons: expands filesystem access toward home directories
path normalization can broaden a named request if not bounded
agent prompt injection and sensitive-file disclosure require fail-closed policy checks

tracking.implementation_plan: Add explicit named-path authorization tests, no-parent/no-recursive expansion tests, and full ACP security review before implementation.

verification: Full SHA and path-expansion diff reviewed; no source implementation made.

entries.title: Allow explicitly named paths in workspace prompt guardrails
entries.rationale: Accept the usability goal, but narrow the wording so a named path is permitted only when available tools and policy allow it, without broadening to parent, neighboring, or recursive paths. Preserve Zion agent wording and compatibility identifiers.
security_reasons: named-path permission must not become blanket absolute-path authorization
prompt content must not expand filesystem scope

tracking.implementation_plan: Adapt base prompt and generated workspace section with bounded named-path wording; add ACP full-target tests and confirm no tool authorization change.

verification: Full SHA and prompt-only security diff reviewed; no source implementation made.
